receiver_contract.role: receiver successor contract/model; production reconstruction still pending

ack_transport.role: one-shot committed Ack delivery / ambiguity successor

assumptions: The console-to-host carrier is ordered within one authenticated connection generation.
A carrier send may fail before write or after bytes may have escaped; the model never infers delivery from a local send result alone.
Receiver application authority resumes only after the committed Ack send reports success; later receiver application messages append behind that Ack on the same ordered reverse stream.
V1 may fail closed and require a fresh authenticated handshake when an old-epoch console application message is already queued ahead of the Ack.
Fresh authenticated handshake creates a new connection generation and discards old-generation queued protocol/application messages.

Cryptographic validity, nonce-domain checks, current-key-only receive, and exact Ack sequence/domain are abstracted as explicit valid/invalid protocol events; this model does not reimplement cryptography.

invariants.property: No reachable state in one connection generation has both peers application-authoritative while their confirmed authority/key epochs differ.
After host begin_send enters DeliveryUnknown, no same-generation carrier success/failure/timeout path restores host Stable except delivery of the exact valid current-transition Ack.
Receiver commit is one-way: receiver epoch is monotonic within a generation, commit reserves/preseals Ack sequence zero, and no Ack-delivery outcome restores the previous receiver epoch.
Ack is the ordered cutover marker: receiver new-epoch application traffic cannot overtake the same epoch Ack on the modeled reverse FIFO.
Proposal/Ack ambiguity, invalid old/wrong-role authority traffic, timeout, and the V1 old-console-message cutover race fail closed rather than guessing a shared epoch.
Replayed Proposal or Ack cannot advance either side twice or restore application authority incorrectly.
Only a fresh authenticated handshake changes connection generation, and it clears all old-generation carrier/rekey state before authority resumes.

claim_boundary: Bounded independent protocol-state composition evidence. It does not prove production Rust equivalence, cryptography, carrier delivery, scheduler behavior, crash/hardware atomicity, Byzantine consensus, or final cross-repository interoperability.
